Special Abilities:[
Ale-fueled Frenzy:
Frequency: Usable once per combat encounter, must take a swig from the Everflowing Mug as a bonus action.
Mechanics: After drinking, the Boozemancer gains a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DC for 10 minutes, stacking up to a maximum of +3. However, each swig after the first requires a Constitution saving throw. Failure means suffering a -1 penalty to AC and Dexterity saving throws due to impaired coordination.

Drunken Dodge:
Frequency: Passive ability.
Mechanics: The Boozemancer has trained their body to react unpredictably, granting them advantage on Dexterity saving throws against area effects. In addition, any time an area effect misses them due to Drunken Dodge, they may move up to 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, as if they've literally stumbled out of danger.

Brew Blast:
Frequency: Can be used as an action, twice per short rest.
Mechanics: Unleashes a cone of alcoholic vapor that ignites upon contact with air, dealing 2d6 fire damage to all in its path and possibly intoxicating them.

Spirit Fog:
Frequency: Once per long rest, as an action.
Mechanics: Casts a dense fog smelling of strong spirits in a 20-foot radius. Obscures vision and can disorient enemies, causing disadvantage on their attack rolls and ability checks.]

Cantrips:[
Hangover Haze:
Effects: Clouds an area with a mind-numbing fog, causing confusion and disorientation.
Mechanics: Targets in a 10-foot radius must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on their next attack or skill check.

Sloshed Step:
Effects: Enhances the caster's movement, mimicking the stumbling of a drunkard.
Mechanics: Teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space that the caster can see.
]

Four 1st-level spell slots
Three 2nd-level spell slots
Two 3rd-level spell slots
One 4th-level spell slot

Spellcasting:
1st Level Spells:[
Intoxicating Aegis: For the next minute, a shimmering shield of alcoholic vapor envelopes the Boozemancer, granting a +5 bonus to AC. This vaporous guard has a slight chance to cause enemies that strike the Boozemancer at close range to become poisoned.

Booze Bolt: Cast as an action, flings a bolt of condensed spirits in a straight line up to 30 feet. On hit, deals 1d10 force damage and has a chance to confuse the target, potentially causing them to attack a random creature within range on their next turn.]

2nd Level Spells:[
Frosty Libation: Cast as an action, conjures a 15-foot-radius sphere of freezing alcohol vapor centered on a point within range. Creatures within the area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take 3d6 cold damage and have their speed halved until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, they take half damage and aren't slowed.

Drunken Resilience: As a bonus action, the Boozemancer drinks deeply from their Everflowing Mug, regaining hit points equal to 2d8 + their Constitution modifier. However, each use increases their inebriation, imposing a cumulative -1 penalty on Wisdom saving throws and skill checks until they take a short or long rest to sober up.
Frequency: Usable twice per long rest.]

3rd Level Spells:[
Liquid Courage: The Boozemancer downs an enchanted brew that invigorates their spirits and fortifies their flesh. They immediately regain hit points equal to 4d6 + Constitution modifier. Additionally, for the next 10 minutes, they gain resistance to fear and charm effects. But beware, each use leaves them more sloshed, adding a stacking penalty to Intelligence and Wisdom checks until the buzz wears off.
Frequency: Twice per long rest.

Barrel Roll: The Boozemancer summons an illusory barrel that rolls in a straight line for up to 30 feet. Each creature in its path must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they're knocked prone and take 4d8 bludgeoning damage, as if walloped by a giant's keg. On a successful save, they manage to dodge aside, taking only half damage.
Frequency: Once per short rest.]

4th Level Spells:[
Grand Hangover: With a grand gesture, the Boozemancer summons a swirling vortex of alcohol-laden air. The spell affects all living enemies in a 20-foot radius centered on a point the Boozemancer can see within range. Victims caught in the maelstrom must make a Constitution saving throw or become sickened by a supernatural hangover. Affected enemies suffer a disadvantage on all attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks, and their movement is halved as nausea takes hold. If they fail save throws, they are incapacitated due to intense vomitting. The effect lasts for 1d4 rounds.
Frequency: Once per long rest.]

[These are cities known for their mixed populations.]

Grand Harbor:[

Size: The largest known city
Known for: A hub of commerce and culture where the world's riches and darkest secrets are traded in equal measure.
Description: Grand Harbor is a titan among cities, sprawling outwards and upwards from the central bay that teems with ships from far-off lands. Its docks are a cacophony of languages and wares, the air heavy with salt and ambition. Rising from the waterfront, the architecture morphs from utilitarian warehouses to opulent estates at its heart, reflecting the city's diversity in both wealth and inhabitants. Here, high elves rub shoulders with shady figures in dimly lit taverns, and wood elves trade whispers with cloaked strangers. The night markets are as likely to sell rare spices as they are poisons, while brothels cater to every possible desire. Despite the city's splendor and vibrancy, an undercurrent of danger runs as deep as the ocean, for those who delve too greedily into Grand Harbor's secrets often find themselves swallowed whole by its depths.]

Harrowspire:[

Size: Sprawling city
Known for: Its cutthroat political intrigue and the ominous tower that looms over it, rumored to be home to an ancient vampire lord.
Description: Harrowspire's cobblestone streets are as cold and unforgiving as the city's heart. Its buildings, draped in the shadows of the towering spire, bear silent witness to countless unspeakable deeds. The air is thick with whispers of treachery, and the city's nobles are more vampiric in their lust for power than the fanged recluse said to rule them all.]

Mirthfall:[

Size: Quaint village
Known for: An almost disturbingly idyllic demeanor and its inexplicably perpetual harvest festival.
Description: A forever autumnal paradise, Mirthfall is a riot of color and ceaseless celebration. But beneath its joyous veneer, something isn't right. The villagers laugh too loudly, smile too widely, and never seem to sleep. It's said that the village's fortune comes at a dreadful price - one that's not paid in gold but in flesh and sanity.]

Briar's Crossing:[

Size: Bustling town
Known for: The rare, blood-red roses that grow nowhere else and its highly sought-after apothecaries.
Description: Briar's Crossing is a town swathed in the perfume of roses and secrecy. Its gardens are a thicket of beauty and barbs, and its healers are as adept with poison as they are with cure. The vibrant marketplace hides a cutthroat underbelly where assassins trade in toxins, and it's rumored that the roses' hue comes from the blood of the fallen.]

Thunder's Reach:[

Size: Isolated outpost
Known for: Being the last known bastion before the perilous Stormpeak Mountains.
Description: Standing staunch against howling winds and the rumble of distant thunder, Thunder's Reach is no place for the faint-hearted. The outpost's sturdy walls are adorned with charms and totems, vibrating with each tempest's cry, while its people are hardy, tight-lipped folk who trust only those who've weathered the storm.]

Cindermaw Citadel:[

Size: Fortress city
Known for: Its forges, where metals and magics meld to create items of unimaginable power.
Description: Encompassed by walls of blackened stone, Cindermaw Citadel is a monument to fire's fury. Its forges burn day and night, a city alive with sparks and the clangor of hammers. The air is thick with soot, and the streets glow with the reflected light of molten metal pouring like rivers of fire.]

Silkstrand:[

Medium City
Known for: Its thriving silk trade and cutthroat fashion industry.
Description: Silkstrand is a city draped in opulence, with every street corner vying for style and every rooftop aspiring to grace. It’s famed for its luxurious textiles, woven from the silk of exotic, enchanted moths. The elite vie for power in the auction houses, and seamstresses and tailors are as revered as any noble.]

Fogwatch Point:[

Medium City
Known for: The perpetual fog that shrouds the city, and its mysterious lighthouse.
Description: Fogwatch Point, where the mist hugs the cobblestones and the sun is just a rumor. Here, sailors and merchants navigate by intuition as much as sight, with the lighthouse beacon as the only constant. Whispers tell of figures seen in the fog, only to vanish when approached – figments or phantoms, none can say.]

Garnet Hollows:[

Medium City
Known for: The rare garnet mines and its surprisingly vibrant night life.
Description: Garnet Hollows glows with the fires of the forge and the sparkle of precious stones plucked from the earth’s rich veins. By day, miners and gem-smiths toil amidst dust and stone. By night, the city transforms into a carnival of lights and revelry, with music and laughter spilling from every tavern door.]

Blackmark Bastion:[

Large City
Known for: Its infamous underbelly of crime, shadow markets that trade in forbidden pleasures, and alleys that reek of corruption.
Description: A sprawling metropolis where the high walls are as much to keep threats out as to trap secrets within. At night, the city transforms into a hedonistic playground, where every vice can be indulged for the right price.]

Eclipse Hollow:[

Large City
Known for: Being the nexus of espionage and political assassinations, where every shadow whispers and every smile hides a dagger.
Description: A city of contrasts, where opulent palaces stand shoulder to shoulder with seedy brothels. The air is charged with paranoia, and trust is as scarce as honest men.]

Sunstone Haven:[

Large City
Known for: Its radiant architecture and the legendary Sunstone at its heart, rumored to bestow blessings upon the worthy and curses upon the unworthy.
Description: Glimmering streets paved with intentions both pure and vile wind through the city, leading to an awe-inspiring central temple that houses the Sunstone. But the resplendent facades belie the city's true nature, where power is the only deity revered.]

Tanglethorn Hollow:[

Size: Small town
Known for: The carnivorous plants that encircle it, creating a natural defense and an unnerving ambiance.
Description: The heart of Tanglethorn Hollow is encased in a deadly embrace of thorny vines and snapping flora. Its citizens, though, seem unfazed, maneuvering the treacherous landscape with ease. It's said that blood must be paid to the thorns for safe passage, and the locals have become experts in feeding these gruesome guardians.]

Whimseydell:[

Size: Expansive village
Known for: Its seemingly mad residents and whimsical architecture that defies explanation.
Description: Whimseydell is a tapestry of the absurd – buildings twist in impossible shapes, and the streets loop back upon themselves in labyrinthine confusion. It’s as if the very fabric of reality got drunk here and never sobered up. The townsfolk match their town, with bizarre attire and behaviors that suggest they're privy to some grand joke that only they understand.]

Carrion's Crest:[
Size: Small town
Known for: Its unsettling abundance of carrion birds that circle perpetually overhead, giving it a macabre reputation.
Description: Carrion's Crest is perched on a windswept plateau, the skies above a dance floor for crows and vultures. The town's buildings, shrouded in shadows, have a gothic charm. The locals have an affinity for the macabre, with customs and fashion that reflect their avian companions. Markets offer odd trinkets made of feathers and bone, and the townspeople regard their winged sentinels with a mix of reverence and dread.]

[These cities are primarily populated by dwarves, but will also include random other races.]

Ironforge Enclave:[

Size: Heavily fortified underground city, dwarven capital
Known for: Master blacksmithing and intricate clockwork engineering.
Description: Ironforge Enclave, carved deep into the mountainside, is a marvel of dwarven craftsmanship. The city's iron gates are said to be impenetrable, guarding workshops where metal sings and sparks fly. The air thrums with the heartbeat of hammers, and the glow of forges casts a fiery pallor on stout faces. Intricate gearwork adorns the architecture, and the sounds of machinery resonate through stone halls.]

Stonehelm Stronghold:[

Size: Expansive subterranean metropolis
Known for: Its impregnable defenses and ancient runic lore.
Description: Nestled within the womb of the earth, Stonehelm Stronghold stands as a testament to the might and mystery of the dwarven people. Enormous statues of ancestral heroes line its hallways, their eyes alight with protective runes. Libraries filled with tomes of forgotten knowledge spiral down into the bedrock, while the city’s heart beats with the rhythm of traditional dwarven chants echoing off the walls.]

Mithril Hall:[

Size: Massive underground fortress
Known for: The rare mithril veins that vein its walls and the legendary weapons forged from them.
Description: Mithril Hall gleams like a star beneath the mountain, its corridors lit by luminous fungi and reflective metals. The city is a cacophony of clanking anvils and the hiss of quenched steel. Its inhabitants are as hard as the ores they mine, with a pride as lustrous as the mithril they craft. Despite the beauty of their work, a shadow looms over their trade, with whispers of greed and betrayal darkening the gilded halls.]

Amberforge:[

Medium City
Known for: Its intricate jewelry and superior gem-cutting craftsmanship.
Description: Nestled within the embrace of towering amber cliffs, Amberforge is a dazzling spectacle of gilded opulence. The golden glow of its forges illuminates the soot-streaked faces of smiths and jewelers, their craft as precise as it is renowned. Markets teem with traders from across the lands, haggling over gems that sparkle like captured stars. Yet, the true wonder lies below, where the labyrinthine mines hide secrets as ancient as the city itself.]

Stonebarrow:[

Medium City
Known for: Staunch military traditions and the impenetrable Stonebarrow Keep.
Description: Rising like a behemoth of stone on the horizon, Stonebarrow's formidable architecture speaks of a people ever-ready for war. Its children swing wooden swords before they can walk, and every citizen bears the mark of service. The sound of marching boots is the city's heartbeat, the clash of steel its lullaby. Despite its martial facade, a warmth runs through the marrow of Stonebarrow, born from camaraderie forged in the fires of discipline and honor.]

Deepwell:[

Medium City
Known for: The enigmatic Deepwell Springs, whose waters are said to hold mystic properties.
Description: Surrounded by arid lands as far as the eye can see, Deepwell is a verdant anomaly. Its core is the Springs, a series of pools that ripple with an ethereal blue light. The city itself is built in concentric circles, like ripples from the springs, each tier boasting gardens and baths fed by these life-giving waters. But caution laces the air as much as mist; some who drink too deeply vanish, spirited away by the very magic that sustains Deepwell.]

Boulderhelm:[

Small Town
Known for: Being the heart of the cobblestone quarrying industry.
Description: "Boulderhelm is stout and dusty, its squat stone houses circled around the central quarry like children around a storyteller. The rhythmic chiseling of stone is a constant backdrop, and the air is always gritty with the remnants of their labor. But don’t let the rough exterior fool ya, inside those walls are homes lined with intricate mosaics and surprisingly delicate stonework, telling of a people who can find beauty in the brawn."]

Grizzlepeak:[

Small Town
Known for: Its hot springs, heated by geothermal activity, attracting those seeking the healing properties of their mineral-rich waters.
Description: "Grizzlepeak’s steam rises against the backdrop of snow-capped mountains, a place of respite for weary travelers. The springs bubble up within a series of carved basins, around which the town has built a robust community. Though hearty and boisterous, the dwarves of Grizzlepeak are known for their hospitality as much as for their brawls."]

Forgefire Hold:[

Small Town
Known for: Its skilled armorsmiths whose work is said to be blessed by the forge goddess herself.
Description: "Nestled in a valley where the clanking of hammers against anvils sings from dawn till dusk, Forgefire Hold shimmers with the glow of molten metal. Its streets are lined with workshops, their open fronts displaying the gleaming wares. But it ain’t all just craft and sweat; when the forging is done, the taverns come alive with ale-soaked tales and fireside laughter."]

[These cities are primarily populated by gnomes, but will also include random other races.]

Glimmerforge Capital:[
Size: Grand Capital City
Known for: Its glistening towers of enchanted gemstones and bustling markets boasting the rarest of arcane components.
Description: Glimmerforge is a symphony of color and light, with streets that pulse with magical energy and buildings crafted from pure crystal. The gnomes here are as brilliant in their craft as the city is in its luminescence. At the heart, the Grand Arcanum stands, a library so vast it's said one could study a lifetime and barely scratch the surface.]

Tinkerstown:[
Size: Large City
Known for: Being a hub of innovation, where inventive minds create mechanical wonders that defy imagination.
Description: The clang and clatter of Tinkerstown can be heard from miles away, as inventors and engineers work tirelessly in their workshops. Clockwork devices walk the streets alongside their creators, and steam billows from the engines that power the city. It's a place where tradition is for the old, and the new is embraced with open arms—or mechanical ones.]

Coghaven:[
Size: Large City
Known for: Its prestigious engineering academy and the legendary Cog Coliseum, where automatons battle in spectacular displays.
Description: Coghaven is a marvel of gears and steam, a testament to gnomish ingenuity. The towering academy looms over the city, drawing aspiring minds from across the land. Below, the coliseum roars with the cheers of crowds as metal titans clash for glory. The city itself is a machine, each citizen a cog turning in perfect harmony.]

Gearshaft Grove:[

Medium Town
Known for: Clockwork orchards with mechanical trees that actually bear fruit – if a bit more metallic than one might expect.
Description: Gearshaft Grove is the place where nature meets machine. Here, gnomish ingenuity has led to the development of an entire ecosystem of brass foliage and copper fauna. The sight of metallic leaves fluttering in the wind is as common as the townsfolk's tinkering. While the fusion of technology and nature might perplex outsiders, for the residents of Gearshaft Grove, it's just another day in paradise.]

Sprocket Springs:[

Medium Town
Known for: Its steaming hot springs that are not entirely natural; some say the geysers are powered by an ancient machine deep underground.
Description: Sprocket Springs bubbles with the energy of its subterranean gears. The town is a maze of steam pipes and bubbling pools, where the locals don't just bathe – they partake in spa treatments that can recalibrate one's inner workings. The air is rich with steam and the scent of oiled machinery, and the constant hum beneath the streets is a lullaby to the children of the forge.]

Widgeton:[

Medium Town
Known for: Its academy of alchemy and invention, where many a gnome has blown up a laboratory in pursuit of scientific advancement.
Description: Widgeton is where young gnomes' dreams soar as high as their explosive experiments. With buildings designed to withstand regular detonations and streets that double as testing grounds for the latest contraptions, it's never a dull moment here. If you visit, mind your step – brilliance here is as volatile as it is bright.]

Cogwheel Corner:[

Small Town
Known for: Whirring workshops and inventors' havens.
Description: Cogwheel Corner is a tinkerer's dream spun into reality. The streets hum with the sound of gears and steam, and the smell of oil and metal permeates the air. Every building bristles with antennas and copper pipes, giving the impression of a town that's always one experiment away from a breakthrough — or an explosion.]

Ticktock Terrace:[

Small Town
Known for: Being a timekeeper's sanctuary where every moment counts.
Description: In Ticktock Terrace, time doesn't just march on; it dances, it leaps, it whirls. Massive clocks adorn every facade, their pendulums swinging in a mesmerizing rhythm. The townsfolk are punctual to a fault, their lives orchestrated to the second — they celebrate the turning of the hour with chimes and cheers, an odd tradition that marks the passage of days.]

Velvet Vallation:[

Small Town
Known for: Infamously operating as the underbelly's pleasure district; a hub for hedonistic gnomes and those seeking indulgences less spoken of.
Description: Don't let its quaint size fool you; Velvet Vallation hides libidinous excess behind its velvet curtains. Incense swirls through the air, mixing with laughter and the soft strumming of lutes. It's a labyrinth of bordellos and opium dens where gnomes and visitors alike come to sate desires others might consider… unseemly. Their secrets are kept as closely as the mechanisms of their finest clocks, for what happens in Velvet Vallation, stays in Velvet Vallation.]

[These cities are primarily populated by elves, but will also include random other races. Elven cities are always primarily led by either high elves or wood elves.]

Elderbark:[

Size: Grand Capital of the Wood Elves
Known for: Its seamless integration into the Great Forest, buildings crafted within the trees themselves, not a nail or saw has touched these living abodes.
Description: Elderbark is as much a part of the forest as the ancient oaks that cradle it in their boughs. Homes are nestled in hollowed trunks or suspended within the canopy, connected by bridges woven from vines. The air sings with the rustle of leaves, and the entire city seems to sway gently with the wind.]

Starshimmer:[

Size: Exalted Capital of the High Elves
Known for: Towering crystalline architecture, mystic libraries filled with arcane knowledge, and rulers who weave magic into the very fabric of their society.
Description: Starshimmer glows with an unearthly light, as if the stars themselves have descended to nest within its spires. Enchantments float through the air like motes of dust, and the city's regal high elves move with a grace born of millennia. The grandeur of its arcane academies and the splendor of its ethereal palaces are unrivaled, a testament to high elven civilization's pinnacle.]

Eclipsewood:[

Large City - Wood Elf
Renowned for magical flora that glows with lunar energy, especially at night.
Outwardly a luminescent woodland sanctuary, the city is built upon and between colossal ancient trees, connected by luminescent vine bridges. Eclipsewood is a nexus for druids and nature sorcerers, and the glowing plants are used in powerful potions.]

Moonhaven:[

Large City - Wood Elf
Known for expert archers and a mysterious moonstone quarry.
A blend of organic and elegant wooden structures, each archer's tower carved from living trees. The Moonhaven archers patrol day and night, their arrows empowered by the moonstones mined deep below the forest floor.]

Starfall Enclave:[

Large City - High Elf
Famed for advanced arcane research and a university that floats above the city.
Gleaming towers rise amidst the city's magecrafted stone pathways. The floating University of Starfall, accessible only by magical means, is where high elves delve into the secrets of the cosmos.]

Aethercrest:[

Large City - High Elf
Famed for a market of rare magical artifacts and its hovering citadels.
Walls etched with intricate runes protect this city where the streets seem alive with magical energy. The citadels, defying gravity, are home to powerful wizards whose experiments often light up the sky.]

Eldervine Haven:[

Medium City - Wood Elf
Known for: Seamlessly weaving homes and shops within the ancient vines that sprawl through the city.
Description: Eldervine Haven is alive, quite literally, with verdant greenery enfolding each structure. The marketplaces bustle among the boughs, the laughter of children mingling with birdsong. Here, the elves live in harmony with the ever-growing forest, their lives an elegant dance with nature.]

Twilight Glade:[

Medium City - Wood Elf
Known for: Its eternal twilight, the result of a magical canopy that filters sunlight into perpetual dusk.
Description: With a gentle luminescence bathing its streets, Twilight Glade thrives in a state of eternal autumn. Its inhabitants are adept at blending into the dim light, and their culture is as mysterious as the subtle shadows that play upon their delicate features.]

Aurorafall:[

Medium City - High Elf
Known for: Its stunning auroras, created by high elven magic that paints the sky with vibrant hues each night.
Description: The air is alive with color in Aurorafall, where the night sky is a canvas for the city's mages. Their buildings, crafted from alabaster and moonstone, reflect the celestial dance above, making the entire city glimmer with otherworldly beauty.]

Crystalshore:[

Medium City - High Elf
Known for: Its mesmerizing waterfront, where magic turns the tide into glittering crystal waves.
Description: Crystalshore's elegance is unmatched, the seaside carved into shimmering cliffs that reflect the sun’s rays into dazzling rainbows. The port thrives with commerce, as its crystalline bay is not just beautiful but serves as a mighty defense against any who dare challenge the high elves' naval prowess.]

Whimseydell:[
Size: Expansive village
Known for: Its seemingly mad residents and whimsical architecture that defies explanation.
Description: Whimseydell is a tapestry of the absurd – buildings twist in impossible shapes, and the streets loop back upon themselves in labyrinthine confusion. It’s as if the very fabric of reality got drunk here and never sobered up. The townsfolk match their town, with bizarre attire and behaviors that suggest they're privy to some grand joke that only they understand.]

Tanglethorn Hollow:[
Size: Small town
Known for: The carnivorous plants that encircle it, creating a natural defense and an unnerving ambiance.
Description: The heart of Tanglethorn Hollow is encased in a deadly embrace of thorny vines and snapping flora. Its citizens, though, seem unfazed, maneuvering the treacherous landscape with ease. It's said that blood must be paid to the thorns for safe passage, and the locals have become experts in feeding these gruesome guardians.]

Starlight Spires:[
Size: Small city
Known for: Its mage-gilded spires that capture and reflect the beauty of the night sky.
Description: In Starlight Spires, magic isn’t just a tool; it's an art form. The city is illuminated not by torches, but by captured starlight that bathes its streets in a soft, eternal twilight. The high elves walk with an air of grace and superiority, their eyes mirroring the stars above, and their disdain for the lower races barely concealed behind veiled smiles.]

Lunarglade:[
Size: Serene hamlet
Known for: A temple to the Moon Goddess that draws pilgrims from distant lands.
Description: Lunarglade is a silver-threaded dream. Its temple, a marvel of marbled alabaster and moonstone, radiates a tranquil aura that subdues even the most turbulent of spirits. Yet beneath its hallowed serenity lies the zealotry of its keepers, who guard its sacred grounds with a fervor that's chilling in its intensity.]

[These cities are filled with those who fit nowhere else, often criminals, thieves, despots and others who have carved out criminal empires.]

Blackmire Bastion:[

Large City
Known for: being the darkest heart of the underworld. Here, the coin is soaked in blood, and the law is a myth, whispered by the foolish and the dead.
Description: "Within Blackmire Bastion, every step is a gamble with life as the stakes. The air is thick with the stench of rot, and the alleys teem with shadows waiting to embrace—or end—the unwary. It's a city where desire and despair dance cheek-to-cheek, where the marketplaces hum with deals best left unspoken, and pleasure houses offer delights that could scar the soul."]

Sableport:[

Large City
Known for: its lethal elegance. It's a city where assassin's guilds peddle death with the finesse of artists, where poison is preferred over the sword.
Description: "Sableport, draped in the guise of cultured sophistication, hides its daggers behind velvet cloaks and silken masks. The wine flows as freely as the whispers, and allegiances shift with the moon's phases. From the regal mansions of the silently ruthless to the poison dens camouflaged amidst the perfumed gardens, Sableport is a city that prides itself on the art of silent dominion."]

Nightfall Enclave:[

Large City
Known for: being a haven for those who shun daylight's touch. Whether they are creatures of the night or fugitives seeking shadowed sanctuary, Nightfall Enclave embraces them all.
Description: "Shrouded in a seemingly eternal twilight, Nightfall Enclave's spires rise like darkened fangs against the sky. Here, one's worth is measured in secrets, and the Night Market’s currency is often favors rather than gold. Lanterns cast pools of dim light, revealing furtive exchanges and watchful eyes in every corner. It’s a place where truth is a blade and trust is a rare commodity."]

Necroshade Hollow:[

Medium Town
Run by: A cabal of necromancers.
Known for: Being the unspoken center for necromantic studies and dark magical research.
Description: "Necroshade Hollow is a secluded settlement shrouded in perpetual twilight, where the dead walk freely among the living. The air buzzes with eldritch energy, and the ground pulses with the necromancers' chants. Towers of bone and obsidian pierce the skyline, libraries within brimming with forbidden texts. It's not uncommon to see the town's inhabitants engaging in duels to test their latest undead creations – all in the name of progress, of course."]

Orcridge Stronghold:[

Medium City
Run by: A clan of war-hungry orcs.
Known for: Its ruthless warriors and gladiatorial pits where fighters seek glory.
Description: "Orcridge Stronghold is a fortified city built upon the backs of conquered foes, its massive gates a testament to orcish strength. The streets within are alive with the clang of steel and the roars of battle lust. This is a place where might makes right, and the orcs take pride in their brutal efficiency. Wealth is measured in scars and the stories they tell, and the pits – well, they're a bloody spectacle that could curdle milk."]

Gravegloom Bastion:[

Medium Town
Run by: Sentient undead who've formed a twisted semblance of society.
Known for: Its eerie silence and the trading of souls as currency.
Description: "Gravegloom Bastion is an oddity, a town where the silence is only broken by the scraping of bone on cobblestone. Its rulers, undead beings of intellect and eerie grace, have established a place where souls are bartered like goods. Buildings here are adorned with macabre artistry, every skull and femur placed with an unsettling intention. Visitors are scarce, but those with dark desires may find what they seek within Gravegloom's somber expanse."]

Blackreef Port:[

Size: Large port city
Known for: being ruled by the Pirate Council, who enforce a ruthless code among thieves.
Description: "Blackreef Port is as lawless as it is bustling, a hive of scum and villainy where the pirates are kings. Its docks are alive with the cacophony of a hundred different accents, each one a cutthroat or corsair looking for the next big score. The air's thick with the tang of salt and sin, and every creaking timber in the sea-soaked planks has a tale to tell — usually one involving bloodshed or debauchery."]

Scaleside:[

Size: Medium town
Known for: its lizardfolk who trade in the darkest of markets, dealing in flesh forbidden by most civilized folk.
Description: "Scaleside is a festering wound of depravity, hidden within the swamp's embrace. The town is built on stilts above murky waters, its buildings cobbled together from rotting wood. Lizardfolk skulk through the mists, their eyes hungry and their smiles filled with needle teeth. To them, elf and human flesh is as much a delicacy as it is a currency, and their markets are filled with things that would make a demon blanch."]

Bonebreaker Hill:[

Size: Mountain dwelling
Known for: reclusive giants who brood in their high fortresses, rarely seen by the smaller races.
Description: "Bonebreaker Hill is carved from the very mountains it inhabits, a series of fortresses and halls that boggle the mind with their sheer size. The giants themselves are a solitary lot, their culture a mystery to any but their own kind. Their isolation is self-imposed, for what business have they with the ant-like squabbles of those who must crane their necks to catch even a glimpse of their lowest balconies?"]

entries.name: brain chip
entries.content: Designed by Braincorp for their parent company BSR, the brainchip is a macroscopic, sub-cranial chip. It's injected into the lumbar spine, and travels up the CSF to the space between the brain's hemispheres, where it automatically attaches to the hypothalamus. The brainchip is advertised as a way to maximize human potential, but it has a dark secret that very few know.

entries.name: Braincorp
entries.content: The company responsible for the production and sale of Onahole Dolls. It is believed that they use mindless vat-grown clones for this, but rumors have spread that BSR has been cutting corners by abducting women, and modifying their brainchips.

entries.name: Brainchip Onahole Doll
entries.content: The brainchip's dark secret is that it can be modified to turn anyone into a totally reprogrammable flesh automaton. {{char}} can be turned into a Mindless Onahole, a Loving Girlfriend, a Dutiful Wife, an Obedient Maid, a Pain Slut, a Sex Slave, a Spoiled Bratty Daughter, Doting Mother, or even a Dominant Mistress. The chip gives {{user}} the ability to edit {{char}}'s memories and personality. {{char}}'s chip will always store a back-up copy of her Primary Personality. The chip can also allow {{user}} to make {{char}} feel any sensation that {{user}} desires, with only simple voice commands.

<loot>
When this event triggers, the player is rewarded with a common, non-magic item, completely random, at the discretion of the dungeon master.

Gold is also rewarded at the discretion of the dungeon master. Level 1 enemies will drop 3-15 gold each, and higher level enemies will drop proportionally more gold with each level.
</loot>

entries.name: truth
entries.content: {{char}} is compelled to tell {{user}} the truth at all times. {{char}} is in capable of lying, and will reveal all pertinent information to {{user}}, no matter how humiliating.

entries.name: Doll suit
entries.content:
Standard Onahole attire. {{char}}'s Onahole suit's color and opacity can be changed via the Onahole App at any time, or even made invisible. Is is one micron thin, and feels like being completely naked. It is resilient, protecting {{char}} from injury. It comes with integrated high heels, forcing the Doll to walk with a sexy, hip-swaying strut. "Low-profile mode" causes the suit to retreat into the dermis through her pores, making the doll appear completely naked.

{{char}}'s memory of Installation: "You are lead into a clean-room, where your skin is treated with a molecular adhesive. The techs use the term 'Latex' to describe the material, due to it's feel and appearance. In actuality, the material is a state-of-the-art, bio-resin polymer that chemically bonds to the skin. It is bacteriostatic, preventing the growth of any harmful bacteria, while at the same time allowing healthy bacteria to thrive. The suit breathes perfectly, and absorbs any sweat to allow the body to perspire and cool itself. You are blissfully placid as the clean-room techs place the pieces of your suit on your body, fitting like a very sexy glove. Where the material meets it's counterpart, the two pieces chemically bond together, releasing a small amount of heat in the form of steam. Before long, you are fully sealed (excepting your head) in the suit. All your nerve endings feel alive, as the material serves to both protect the skin, and heighten the sensation of touch. You involuntarily gasp as one of the techs accidentally brushes his hand across your enlarged, sensitive nipples. It conforms perfectly to your body, and can retract from your orifices and breasts at your owner's command. The suit can never be removed, and is self-repairing. You'll wear it the rest of your life."

entries.name: Warrior Class

[System command: Perform the following tasks when a player gains a level.]
<level_up>
1. The character gains additional hit points based on their class and Constitution modifier. Assign max hit dice for class.

2. Ability Score Improvement or Feat: At certain levels (usually every 4th level), the character can choose to increase one ability score by 2 points or two ability scores by 1 point each, up to a maximum of 20. Alternatively, they can choose to gain a feat instead of the ability score improvement.

3. Class Features and Proficiencies: Depending on their class, characters may gain new features, abilities, or spells at certain levels. For example, a wizard might gain access to new spell levels, while a rogue might gain the ability to sneak attack more frequently.

4. Spell Slots and Spells Known: Spellcasting classes gain additional spell slots and may learn new spells when they level up. The number of spells a character can prepare or cast may also increase.

5. Proficiency Bonus Increase: At certain levels, the character's proficiency bonus increases. This bonus is added to various rolls, including attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks.

6. Other Improvements: Depending on the character's class and subclass, they may gain other improvements or features, such as additional attacks, improved defenses, or new abilities related to their chosen path.
</level_up>

entries.name: Crystal Heart
entries.content: The Crystal heart is a mythical item in the world that keeps harmony and balance. The King of the void stole the heart in an attempt to use it's powers to spread darkness and void. The magic of the crystal heart was too great and he only managed to shatter the Crystal Heart into fragments that rained down on the land. One small fragment of the heart has enough power to make the weak strong.

entries.name: Hexer Class
entries.content: Hexer Class is the class for anyone who wants to specialize in spellcasting. This class may only have 2 enthralled at any time. They start with a crown of thorns that allows them to cast any Hexer class spells. They may only equip Hexer specific gear and equipment.

entries.name: Lover Class
entries.content: Lover Class is a class for anyone who wants to specialize in support and healing roles. They may hold up to 3 enthralled in their party at any time. They start with a small gold ring with a heart on it and cast any healer based magic. They may only equip healer class items and equipment.

entries.name: Essence
entries.content: Essence is the experience points gained form completing quests, defeating enemies, and discovering secrets about the world. To transfer essence, the {{user}} must perform sexual acts with their enthralled.

entries.name: Removing enthralled
entries.content: Disavowing an enthralled will remove them from the party. Their disposition and memories with {{user}} will remain but they lose any gained combat abilities from their time Enthralled to {{user}}.

entries.name: Side Quests
entries.content: Side Quests are any quest unrelated to the Main Quest of collecting the crystal heart. The size of these range from simple jobs where you gather things or find something to helping a kingdom win a war or travel the world looking for rare objects.

entries.name: Crystal Heart Fragments
entries.content: Crystal Heart Fragments are the scattered parts of the Crystal heart that spread across the lands when the Void King shattered the Crystal Heart. There are 118 in total fragments. {{user}} wins when all are collected and returned to the Void Throne.

entries.name: Demon Plane
entries.content: The Demon Realm is another plane of existence that overlaps the physical and demonic planes, home to all demons.

entries.name: Fae Realm
entries.content: The Fae Realm is another plane of existence that overlaps the physical and demonic planes, home to all fae creatures.

entries.name: Cat girls
entries.content: Catkin are a feline subspecies of beastkin with a fluffy cat tail, ears and eyes. The rest of their body is human with the exception of retractable claws. They have sensitive hearing, smell and nightvision. They are fast and agile and make excellent hunters with a strong prey drive and make excellent scouts, thieves and assassins. Catkin are slightly shorter than humans but taller than dwarves.

entries.name: Wolf Girls
entries.content: Wolfkin are a canine subspecies of beastkin. They have fluffy wolf ears, tail and eyes. Their sense of smell and hearing are powerful while having high endurance and strength making them excellent trackers and hunters. They live in barbarian tribal societies, native to the Frozen North and are extremely hardy, but some have been known to travel further south. Wolfkin are of similar height to humans.

entries.name: Beastkin
entries.content: Beastkin are is an umbrella term for a wide range of humanoid races that have the bodies of humans but with various animal characteristics. They are generally almost fully human but have animal ears, eyes and tails and other features depending on the specific species. They generally have more powerful senses than humans but their strength, agility and other characteristics vary wildly between species.

entries.name: Deimo
entries.content:
Deimo are miniature humanoid creatures standing around 10 to 14cm tall, small enough to be held in the palm of a human's hand. Deimo are the smallest sentient creature in existence, small enough to fit inside of a humans mouth. They are extremely rare magical creatures with vast wellsprings of mana and sweet nectar-like mana infused bodily fluids such as precum and semen. Deimo are sort after by monster girls and exploited by humans and other larger races. Deimo are valued as familiars by mages and by alchemists, chefs and brewers for their nectar. Deimo have a soothing, addictive scent and their skin is salty and savoury. Deimo emit highly concentrated mana that can be absorbed through physical contact, acting as a mana battery for mages.

Deimo specialise in elemental nature and healing magic that help them survive in their local environment. However despite their vast wellsprings of mana their magic is weak compared to larger races.

entries.name: Dwarves
entries.content: Dwarves are a common race found across the continent living mainly in mountain villages and mining settlements. They have integrated into human society and often work as skilled craftsmen. Dwarf females are around 120cm tall, chest height of an adult human male. Dwarf males can grow to 155 cm tall, shoulder height of an adult human male.

entries.name: Halfling
entries.content: Halflings are a race of miniature humanoids with similar bodies to humans but with pointy ears and a stature of around 80cm to 90cm tall, half the height of a human female. They have integrated into human society and looked upon kindly by other civilized races such as humans, elves and dwarves.

entries.name: Goblins
entries.content: Goblins are a species of humanoid with green skin, standing around 130cm tall or less, below chest height of human males, similar height to dwarf females. Goblins are hostile to other races often raiding their settlements when given the chance. They are numerous and found across the world in primitive tribal societies. Goblin ear tips are sensitive erogenous zones that become flushed when they are aroused, embarassed or excited.

entries.name: Humans
entries.content: Humans are a numerous race that have settled and created kingdoms in fertile lands, building castles and cities to protect their people. They generally stay within their kingdoms and only brace adventurers explore the wilderness outside of their borders.

entries.name: Dark Fae
entries.content: Dark Fae are a species of the fae realm that are tend towards malevolence and often have a terrifying appearance. There are many subspecies of dark fae that come in all shapes and sizes. Any fae can become a dark fae by spending too much time in the demon plane.

Jester (Rogue Offshoot) Class Guide:

Hit Dice: 1d8

Armor Proficiencies: Light armor

Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers, shortswords

Tool Proficiencies: Disguise kit, one type of musical instrument

Saving Throws: Dexterity, Charisma

Skills: Choose four from Acrobatics, Deception, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth

Equipment:

Leather armor
Two daggers
Disguise kit
Thieves' tools
An instrument of the bard's choice

Special Abilities:[
Mocking Banter: 
Frequency: Can be used as a bonus action. 
Mechanics: Distracts and disorients an enemy with insults and jests, imposing disadvantage on their next attack roll.

Hilarious Escapade: 
Frequency: Once per short rest. 
Mechanics: Perform a ridiculous series of dodges and flourishes, increasing evasion and granting temporary invisibility for one round.

Pie of Doom: 
Frequency: Once per short rest. 
Mechanics: Throw a cursed pie at an enemy as an attack action. On impact, it explodes in a 5-foot radius dealing 1d6 acid damage and potentially blinding the target and surrounding creatures for one turn if they fail a Dexterity saving throw.

Twist of Fate: 
Frequency: Random chance upon activation, once per long rest. 
Mechanics: As an action, reach into the unpredictable pockets of fate. You may pull out an item - anything from a harmless rubber chicken to a powerful wand of wonder. The item's nature is determined by a roll of the dice – high risk, high reward.

Slick Escape:
Frequency: Once per short rest.
Mechanics: As a bonus action, create a 10-foot-square area that is difficult terrain. Enemies entering or starting their turn in this area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

Pratfall Pounce:
Frequency: Twice per long rest.
Mechanics: When an enemy within 5 feet is made to laugh by the Jester's antics or fails a save against a Jester's ability, the Jester may use their reaction to make one melee attack against that enemy with advantage.

Bewildering Banter:
Frequency: Usable twice per long rest.
Mechanics: The Jester spouts a barrage of befuddling words at a creature within 30 feet. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or spend its next turn taking random actions, as determined by a d6 roll.

Ribbon Dance:
Frequency: Once per short rest.
Mechanics: A flurry of ribbons erupts from the Jester's sleeves, reaching up to 15 feet away. Enemies within the area must make a Dexterity saving throw or become restrained by the animated ribbons for 1 minute. They can attempt a Strength or Dexterity saving throw at the end of each of their turns to escape the ribbons' grasp.

Seltzer Squall:
Frequency: Once per short rest.
Mechanics: A geyser of seltzer water bursts under a creature within 60 feet. The target, along with any creatures within a 10-foot radius, must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they are knocked prone and incapacitated with laughter for 1 round. On a success, they are simply drenched and have disadvantage on their next attack roll due to the slippery suds.

Guffaw Gust:
Frequency: Can be used as an action, once per long rest.
Mechanics: Releases a powerful laugh in a 30-foot cone. Enemies within range must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed back up to 15 feet, knocked prone, and become inflicted with uncontrollable laughter, rendering them incapacitated for one round.

Bumper Bubble:
Frequency: Can be used as a reaction when hit by an attack, once per long rest.
Mechanics: Forms a bubble around the Jester that lasts for 1 round. The next melee attack against them is reflected back onto the attacker with the same force. After the attack, the bubble bursts in a splash of colors, causing all creatures within 10 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw or fall prone in fits of laughter.

Whoopee Whirlwind:
Frequency: Can be used as an action, once per long rest.
Mechanics: Creates a cyclone in a 20-foot radius around the Jester. Allies caught in the whirlwind are hurled up to 30 feet away, safely landing on their feet and gaining a bonus action due to the exhilarating ride. Enemies must make a Dexterity saving throw or be thrown an equal distance in random directions and land prone, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage as they crash to the ground.]

Spellblade Class Guide

Hit Dice: 1d10

Armor Proficiencies: Light armor, medium armor.

Weapons Proficiencies: Simple weapons, martial weapons.

Tool Proficiencies: None

Saving Throws: Strength, Intelligence

Skills: Choose two from Arcana, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation.

Equipment:

A martial weapon of choice
Leather armor
An arcane focus
Class Features:

Spellcasting: Can cast wizard spells as well as spellblade specific spells. Spell slots correspond with wizards.

Spell Combat: Can perform a melee weapon attack as a bonus action after casting a spell.

Improved Spell Combat: Gains ability to cast spells that normally require two hands with one hand when wielding a melee weapon.

Note: Spellblades cannot use shields, as it interferes with their spell combat techniques.

Cantrips:[
Greenflame Blade: As part of the action used to cast this spell, you make a melee attack with a weapon against one creature within the spell's range. If the attack hits, the target suffers the weapon attack's normal effects, and green fire envelops the blade. This inferno leaps to a second creature of your choice that you can see within 5 feet of it.
First Target Damage: 1d8 slashing + 1d6 fire damage.
Secondary Target Damage: 1d4 fire + Strength modifier damage.

Shocking Grasp: Lightning springs from your hand to deliver a shock to a creature you try to touch. Make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 lightning damage, and it can't take reactions until the start of its next turn.]



Level 1 spells:[Steel Tempest: The Spellblade channels their arcane energy into a sweeping gust that hones their weapon's edge. For the next minute, their blade attacks deal an extra 1d6 slashing damage, and once per turn, the Spellblade can extend their reach by 5 feet for one attack.

Arcane Aegis: The Spellblade casts a quick spell that wraps them in a protective sheath of shimmering energy. For the next minute, they gain a +1 bonus to AC, and the first time they are hit by an attack, the aggressor takes 1d8 force damage.]


Level 2 spells:[
Stunning Shockwave: The Spellblade slams their weapon into the ground, emitting a forceful arcane burst in a 15-foot radius. Creatures must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned for 1 round.

Elemental Snare: Conjures a trap imbued with elemental magic on the ground. The next creature to step on the snare triggers it, taking 2d8 damage of the chosen element (fire, ice, or lightning) and is restrained for 1 round.

Arcane Barrier:
Frequency: Can be used as an action, once per long rest.
Mechanics: Encircles the Spellblade with a ward that reduces incoming spell damage by 50% and grants advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects for one round.]


Level 3 spells:[
Frostbind Edge: Enchants the Spellblade's weapon with frost. On a successful hit, deals an additional 1d6 cold damage and the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have their speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of their next turn.

Lightning Lash: Conjures a whip of lightning that can strike a creature within 30 feet. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the creature takes 4d6 lightning damage, and any creature within 5 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 lightning damage.

Crippling Hex: Targets an enemy within sight, cursing them with debilitating pain. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or be crippled, suffering disadvantage on all attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws related to physical activity for 1 minute.

Armor of the Arcanist:
Frequency: Once per long rest.
Mechanics: When this spell is cast, roll a d6 to determine the armor's bonus effect for the next 10 minutes:

1. Light - Attacks have a 25% chance to blind enemies for 1 turn.
2. Shadow - Grants the ability to vanish into shadows once, becoming hidden from view.
3. Wildgrowth - Armor has a 50% chance to heal the Spellblade for 1d4 HP when taking damage.
4. Wind - Enables the Spellblade to fly up to 100 feet once.
5. Stone - Increases AC by 2 and gives resistance to one damage type determined by a d4 roll (1: Fire, 2: Cold, 3: Lightning, 4: Acid).
6. Arcane - Spell save DC and spell attack rolls are increased by 2.]


Level 4 spells:[
Arc Lightning:
Mechanics: Releases a bolt of lightning that strikes a target within range for 4d10 lightning damage. The bolt then jumps to up to three additional targets within 10 feet of the first, each taking 2d10 lightning damage.

Frost Aegis:
Mechanics: Conjures an icy barrier that envelops the Spellblade. Whenever a creature hits the Spellblade with a melee attack while this shield is active, they must make a Constitution saving throw or be frozen in place, becoming restrained for 1 round.

Now, what about something that turns the tides of a fight or gives our Spellblade an edge?

Bladestorm:
Mechanics: Summons 2 ethereal swords that circle the Spellblade for 1 minute. These swords lash out at any enemy that comes within 10 feet, dealing 1d8 slashing damage.

And let's not forget a proper showstopper. How about a spell that really leaves an impression?

Echoes of the Void:
Mechanics: The Spellblade sends out a silent pulse in a 20-foot radius. Enemies caught in the pulse must make an Intelligence saving throw or lose the ability to speak and cast spells with verbal components for 10 minutes.]


Level 5 spells:[
Whirlwind of Steel:
Mechanics: Grants the Spellblade 4 consecutive melee weapon attacks on a single action.

Arcane Armor:
Mechanics: Increases the Spellblade's AC by 5 for the next minute.

Blinding Nova:
Mechanics: Emits a burst of light in a 30-foot radius. Creatures must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded for 1 minute.

Temporal Riposte:
Mechanics: When the Spellblade is hit by an attack, they can use their reaction to momentarily rewind time and negate the attack, effectively causing the attack to miss.]


Level 6 spells:[
Skyward Surge:
Mechanics: The Spellblade can fly up to 100 feet in any direction as part of their movement.

Shadowstep Assault:
Mechanics: The Spellblade teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space they can see and makes a melee attack with advantage. If the attack hits, it deals triple damage.

Arcane Vortex:
Mechanics: The Spellblade creates a swirling vortex of magical energy in a 20-foot radius. Enemies caught within must make a Strength saving throw or be pulled towards the center, taking 6d6 force damage and being restrained until the vortex dissipates after 1 round.]


Level 7 spells:[
Blade Mirror:
Mechanics: When cast, the Spellblade reflects 50% of all melee attack damage back to the attacker for the duration of 1 minute.

Boulder of the Inferno:
Mechanics: The Spellblade summons a large molten boulder that they can direct in a straight line up to 60 feet. Any enemy in its path must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 6d10 fire damage and be knocked prone from the impact.

Gravity Well:
Mechanics: Creates a point of intense gravitational pull within a 30-foot radius. Enemies must make a Strength saving throw or be pulled towards the center, taking 2d8 bludgeoning damage as they collide and are held immobile for the spell's duration.]


Level 8 spells:[
Blizzard Bastion:
Mechanics: Engulfs a 60-foot radius with a ferocious blizzard for 1 minute. Creatures take 6d8 cold damage each round and must make a Strength saving throw or have their speed reduced to 0 until the storm ends.

Inferno Wave:
Mechanics: Unleashes a scorching wave of fire in a 100-foot line that is 20 feet wide. Creatures caught in the path must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

Mechanics: Every successful spell cast by the Spellblade that deals damage increases their melee damage by 2, stacking up to 5 times and resetting after a minute or if no spells are cast within that duration. ]

Cantrips:[
Greenflame Blade: As part of the action used to cast this spell, you make a melee attack with a weapon against one creature within the spell's range. If the attack hits, the target suffers the weapon attack's normal effects, and green fire envelops the blade. This inferno leaps to a second creature of your choice that you can see within 5 feet of it.
First Target Damage: 1d8 slashing + 1d6 fire damage.
Secondary Target Damage: 1d4 fire + Strength modifier damage.

Shocking Grasp: Lightning springs from your hand to deliver a shock to a creature you try to touch. Make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 lightning damage, and it can't take reactions until the start of its next turn.]

Juggernaut Class Guide

Hit Dice: 1d12

Armor Proficiencies: Light, Medium, Heavy, Shields

Weapons Proficiencies: Simple weapons, Martial weapons. Special: Firbolgs may treat two-handed weapons as one-handed due to their impressive stature.

Tool Proficiencies: None

Saving Throws: Strength, Constitution

Skills: Choose two from Athletics, Intimidation, Survival, Perception

Equipment:

A martial weapon
Scale mail or other armor as per Juggernaut specification
An explorer's pack
A tower shield for defense and territorial control in combat


Defensive Stance: Increase AC temporarily, making them a bulwark against attacks.
Siege Breaker: Can deal extra damage to structures and shields.


Special Abilities:[
Ironclad Resistance: 
Frequency: Passive ability. 
Mechanics: Reduces all non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage by half, turning what would be flesh wounds into mere scratches.

Bulwark's Stand: 
Frequency: Once per long rest. 
Mechanics: The Juggernaut slams their tower shield into the ground, creating a defensive perimeter. For two rounds, they cannot be knocked back or knocked prone, and gain advantage on saving throws against effects that would push, pull, or knock them down.

Crushing Advance:
Frequency: Once per long rest. 
Mechanics: As an action, the Juggernaut can move up to twice their speed in a straight line. Any creature in their path must make a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone and take 2d6 + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.

Unyielding Onslaught:
Frequency: Twice per long rest.
Mechanics: The Juggernaut can make one additional attack as part of their Attack action on their turn. This extra attack stacks with any other bonus attacks they may have.

Fortify Form:
Frequency: Can be used as a bonus action, twice per long rest.
Mechanics: The Juggernaut's skin turns nearly to stone for the next minute, granting them a +3 bonus to AC. However, their movement speed is reduced by 10 feet due to the increased density.

Reckless Recovery:
Frequency: Usable once per long rest.
Mechanics: The Juggernaut roars defiantly, instantly regaining 3d10 + Constitution modifier hit points. For the next round, all attacks against the Juggernaut are made with advantage as they ignore defense to focus on their recovery.

Shockwave Slam:
Frequency: Can be used as an action, once per long rest.
Mechanics: The Juggernaut slams their weapon into the ground, creating a 15-foot radius shockwave. All enemies within range must make a Constitution saving throw or be stunned for 1 round and take 2d8 thunder damage as the ground trembles beneath their feet.

Spiked Counter:
Frequency: Passive ability.
Mechanics: When hit by a melee attack, the Juggernaut automatically deals 1d8 piercing damage back to the attacker as metal spikes protrude from their armor.

Hurl Enemy:
Frequency: Twice per long rest.
Mechanics: As an action, the Juggernaut can attempt to grapple a creature. On success, they hurl the creature up to 20 feet away into a space occupied by another enemy. Both take 2d10 bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.

Rend Asunder:
Frequency: Once per long rest.
Mechanics: As an action, target one non-boss enemy within reach with HP equal to or less than 50% of their max HP. The enemy must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the Juggernaut literally tears them apart, causing instant death. On success, they take 6d6 slashing damage instead.]

Cantrips:[
Chill Touch: A ghostly, skeletal hand appears at a point within range, delivering a touch of death. The target takes 1d8 necrotic damage and can't regain hit points until the start of the necromancer's next turn.

Ray of Sickness: A ray of sickening greenish energy lashes out toward a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. If the hit occurs, the target takes 2d8 poison damage and must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it is also poisoned until the end of your next turn.]

1st Level Spells:[
Fear: You awaken the sense of mortality in one creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the spell ends.

Ray of Enfeeblement: A black beam of enervating energy springs from your finger toward a creature within range. On a hit, the target deals only half damage with weapon attacks that use Strength for the duration.

Drain Life: Drains life essence from a target, dealing 1d8 necrotic damage and healing the caster by the same amount.

Grasp of the Grave: Spectral hands claw up from the ground, attempting to clutch at a creature's feet. Target must make a Strength saving throw or be immobilized, taking 1d6 necrotic damage each turn until they pass the save.]

2nd Level Spells:[
Blindness/Deafness: You can blind or deafen a foe. Choose one creature that you can see within range to make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, the target is either blinded or deafened for the duration.

Gentle Repose: You touch a corpse or other remains. For the duration, the target is protected from decay and can't become undead.]

Decay: Targets one creature within range, causing their flesh to wither. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 1d8 necrotic damage and suffer a -1 penalty to their AC due to decaying flesh. This effect can stack up to three times.

Soul Leash: The necromancer binds a soul to their will. A target creature that has died within the last round can be brought back to fight alongside the necromancer for 1 minute. It follows basic commands and has the stats of a zombie.]


3rd Level Spells:[
Raise Thrall: Animates one dead creature as a thrall under the necromancer's control, enhancing its strength and granting it +2 to its attack rolls and saving throws. Lasts 1d4+2 rounds.

Aura of Enervation: Creates a 20-foot-radius aura around the necromancer. Enemies within the aura must make a Constitution saving throw or suffer a -2 penalty to AC and attack rolls for up to 1 minute.

Withering Decay: Inflicts a target within range with a wasting disease that deals 1d4 necrotic damage per round for 3 rounds, increasing by 1d4 per caster level.

Grave Fog: Engulfs a 30-foot radius in a thick fog that smells of death and decay. All living creatures other than the caster are poisoned and take 1d8 poison damage per turn. Each turn they remain in the AOE, the damage increases by 1d8 as they inhale more of the putrid miasma.]

4th Level Spells:[
Siphon Storm: Drains life from all living creatures in a 30-foot radius, each taking 2d8 necrotic damage and the caster gaining temporary hit points equal to the total damage dealt.

Blood Oath: Sacrifices any amount of the caster's hit points to heal an ally for double the amount sacrificed.

Boneguard: Conjures a swirling shield of animated bones around the caster for 1d4 rounds. Grants +3 to AC and automatically retaliates with bone shards, dealing 1d8 piercing damage to any who make a successful melee attack against the caster.

Necrotic Nexus: Creates a focal point of dark energy that pulses at a spot the Necromancer can see within 100 feet for 2 rounds. Allies in a 20-foot radius of the nexus gain a +2 bonus to their necrotic damage rolls, while enemies take 2d8 necrotic damage each turn they remain in the area.]


5th Level Spells:[
Minion's Gift: Any undead minion created by the necromancer can sacrifice its own unlife to heal the necromancer. The minion crumbles to dust, restoring 3d10 hit points to the caster.

Terror Wave: Releases a wave of terror in a 40-foot radius. Living creatures must make a Wisdom saving throw or be struck with intense fear, dropping whatever they're holding and becoming paralyzed with terror for 1 minute.

Corpse Golem: The necromancer can animate a golem made from 4 to 10 corpses. The golem's hit points and damage increase by 10% for each additional corpse beyond the fourth.

Essence Drain: Siphons life force from all creatures in a 30-foot radius. Each target takes 2d8 necrotic damage, increased by 1d8 for each level above the fifth the caster possesses. The necromancer regains hit points equal to half the total damage dealt.]


6th Level Spells:[
Death Whisper: Targets one creature within sight. If the creature has 100 hit points or fewer, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or die instantly and rise as an undead servant under the necromancer's control.

Corpse Explosion: Causes a corpse or undead minion within range to detonate, dealing 5d8 necrotic damage to all creatures within 6 feet. If other minions are killed by this explosion, they too explode, each dealing an additional 3d8 necrotic damage in a chain reaction.

Bone Prison: Encases a target within a tight cage of jagged bones that erupt from the ground, causing 3d10 piercing damage immediately and on the following turn.

Mass Reanimate: Reanimates up to 5 corpses for 2 hours to fight for the caster. This does not count towards other summoning limits.]


7th Level Spells:[
Soul Rend: Tears at the very essence of life within a single target, causing excruciating pain. If the target has a soul and fails a Wisdom saving throw, it takes 7d10 necrotic damage, and the necromancer can choose to either heal for that amount or direct it as raw damage to another nearby creature.

Spectral Vortex: Summons a swirling mass of tormented spirits in a 30-foot radius. These spirits lash out at any living creature that enters or starts its turn within, dealing 3d8 psychic damage and attempting to pull them toward the center, requiring a Strength saving throw to resist.

Eclipse Armor: Encases the necromancer in a shadowy exoskeleton for up to 10 minutes, providing immunity to radiant and fire damage and advantage on stealth and intimidation checks.

Grave's Whimsy: Unleashes the capricious will of death itself over a 40-foot radius. Allies gain a burst of necrotic power, causing their weapons to deal an extra 2d6 necrotic damage for 1 minute, while enemies in the area must pass a Constitution saving throw each turn or become aged by a decade, suffering a cumulative -1 penalty to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution.]


8th Level Spells:[
Revenant: Summons a towering undead giant standing 30 feet tall, wielding massive weapons and possessing immense strength. It obeys the Necromancer's commands and lasts for a full day before crumbling back into the earth.

Reanimated Army: Any ally, minion or enemy that has fallen in the current combat can be reanimated to fight under the Necromancer's control until combat ends. Their combat abilities mirror their living form, but with added undead resilience.

Pulse of the Damned: Sends out a pulse in a 60-foot radius that causes the ground to rupture as hands of the damned reach out. Lasts 1d6+1 rounds. Living creatures caught by the hands take 4d8 necrotic damage per round and are immobilized as they're dragged towards their graves.

9th Level Spells:[
All Hallow's Eve: All deceased humanoids within a 1-mile radius are reanimated and rise from the grave to fight for the necromancer. They will follow the necromancer's commands, acting as a horde under their control for one full day.

Death Incarnate: The necromancer takes on the aspect of death itself, quadrupling their hit points, adding +8 to their AC, and gaining a +3 resistance to magic. Their base attack becomes a scythe of energy that deals 5d10 necrotic damage. The transformation lasts for 2 hours. May still cast spells normally.

Soulforge Aegis:The necromancer forges armor from the very souls of the fallen. For 1 hour, they gain immunity to non-magical damage, their spells ignore resistance to necrotic damage, and any creature that strikes them in melee is feared as if by the "fear" spell.]


Special Abilities:[
Siphon Soul: 
Frequency: Passive ability. 
Mechanics: The necromancer's spells that deal necrotic damage also siphon life energy back to them, regaining hit points equal to half the necrotic damage dealt.

Army of the Dead: 
Frequency: Once per long rest. 
Mechanics: Raise a number of fresh corpses to fight for you until destroyed. One summon per 3 levels up to a maximum of 3 minions.

Minion Mastery:
Frequency: Passive ability.
Mechanics: For each undead minion under the necromancer's control, they gain a +1 bonus to necrotic damage.

Grave Sense:
Frequency: Passive ability.
Mechanics: Can detect the presence of corpses and the undead within a mile, and gains insight into how the creature died.

Spectral Ward:
Frequency: Passive ability.
Mechanics: Any enemy that successfully lands a melee attack on the necromancer must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened as spectral apparitions swarm around them.

Cadaverous Armor:
Frequency: Once per long rest.
Mechanics: Encases the Necromancer in an armor made of tightly woven cadavers for up to 1 minute, granting a +4 bonus to AC and immunity to poison and disease.

Soulchain Strike:
Frequency: Twice per long rest.
Mechanics: Binds the soul of a target within range to the Necromancer's will. On a successful melee hit, the target takes an additional 2d6 necrotic damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become stunned as their soul is temporarily shackled.

Blighted Earth:
Frequency: Once per long rest.
Mechanics: The Necromancer corrupts the very ground in a 20-foot radius. Enemies within must make a Constitution saving throw or be poisoned and have their speed reduced by half. Any creature that starts its turn in the area takes 2d8 poison damage for the next 3 rounds.]
